sources.title: Recharge writer and reviewer aggregation oracles
Independent source-first review after audit remediation

claims.text: Source asks for recharge DDL and recent-month highest cumulative recharge user but leaves dialect, schema, status, window and tie semantics unspecified.
Under the declared contract, countable rows in a half-open rolling-month window are grouped by user and summed before top-user ordering.
Fixed-point money semantics and the half-open rolling-month definition are explicit answer-side choices, with natural-month semantics called out separately.
Independent fixtures validate success filtering, window boundaries, aggregation, ranking input and empty-window behavior.

validation.reported_stdout: PASS writer and reviewer recharge oracles

findings: Source preserves DDL plus a recent-month highest cumulative recharge-user query, but not dialect/schema/status/window/tie conventions.
Candidate explicitly separates those conventions as answer-side choices instead of recovered facts.
DDL models identity,user,amount,status,payment time and creation time; fixed-point amount semantics are appropriate while exact precision is stated as an example.
Query correctly filters the countable rolling-month rows before grouping, sums amount per user, then orders aggregate totals; pre-aggregation LIMIT would be wrong.
Half-open [start,end) window is coherent and candidate distinguishes it from a natural-calendar-month contract.
Deterministic user_id tie-breaker is explicitly answer-side; returning every tied winner would require a different query.
Independent writer/reviewer fixtures verify success filtering, both time boundaries, aggregation, outside-window exclusion and empty-window behavior.

The earlier audit finding was remediated before this fixed-blob review: DDL is presentation text rather than an executable SELECT parser input, and a non-source database-brand anchor was removed from the core conclusion.
